1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l73.c13/t:
Order!

Richard M Nixon, how do you plead on 1 count of treason against the United States of America, 1 count of misappropriation of campaign funds, 1 count of obstruction of justice, one count of abuse of power, one count of…

Richard Nixon, as he heard all this droning from the judge, closed his eyes, waiting for the sentence to end. He had been up all night, unable to sleep due to all the stress from the trial. Before he knew it, he’d fallen unconscious. All of a sudden, he jolted awake to the sound of the judge screaming; "NIXON! What do you plead?..."

"Uh, not guilty, your honour… not guilty?"

"On 1 count of sleeping in a court of law?..."

"When did you say tha- actually yes, your honour. The liberal media has been painting an askew picture of me. I was merely resting my eyes."
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l77.c14/t:
Hubert Humphrey's inauguration address, January 20th, 1969.

Today I have stood, where once Abraham Lincoln stood and took an oath to my country. It is very appropriate then that from this bastion of America, this very heart of the great men who created the principles of freedom in this country, that today we sound the drum for freedom as have our generations of forebears before us done, time and time again through history. Let us rise to the call of freedom-loving blood that is in us and send our answer to the tyranny that clanks its chains upon the Negro. In the name of the greatest country that has ever trod this earth, I draw the line in the dust and toss the gauntlet before the feet of tyranny . . . and I say . . . desegregation today . . . desegregation tomorrow . . . desegregation forever!
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l93.c27/t: The murders and rioting in America will be your first order of business, and more long term, the war on Vietnam. If both of those are dealt with, your silent majority will be pleased. Other than that, inflation must be dealt with, as well as the excess of Great Society. Good luck, and welcome back to the executive branch!
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l95.c32/t: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your performance in debates and campaigning were widely praised compared to 1960, which allowed you to win with a massive landslide. What a turnaround from 1964!
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l97.c32/t: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your lead dwindled a bit as Wallace’s appeal dampened, but your coalition managed to remain intact.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l100.c32/: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. The bombing halt and Wallace collapsing in the north nearly lost you the election, but you managed to hang on.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l103.c33/: For the first time since 1888, the winner of the electoral vote lost the popular vote. It seems many people underestimated how much of an effect Wallace had on your campaign in the south.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l106.c27/: After your second loss in a presidential election, your chances of being renominated for the presidency, or ANYTHING for that matter is nearly zero. Retirement and an elder statesman position are all that will await you. It seems Americans will once and for all not have Nixon to kick around…
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l108.c32/: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 7 of the last 9 presidential elections. With the margins being as close as 8 years ago, you are already having flashbacks of 1960.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l111.c32/: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 8 of the last 10 presidential elections. Somehow you managed to do worse compared to 1960. Nobody is quite sure how that is even possible, but suffice it to say you will receive much of the blame.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l113.c32/: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 8 of the last 10 presidential elections. Not only did you lose, but you got crushed. Under the weight of two ideologically different candidates, your moderate positions seemed to not appeal. If the skirmish between liberal and conservative republicans wasn’t already bad, it was going to get a lot worse after this.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l117.c33/: At the end of the day, in possibly the most shocking turn of events, the popular vote fell in your favour. Nobody is sure what to make of this, but maybe the Democrats can use their house and senate supermajorities, combined with disaffected Republicans, to pass electoral reform?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l122.c27/: A return to the Senate might be in order, so you might defend liberalism from demise during Nixon's administration, or gearing up for a run in 1972. perhaps you can do both. In any case, let's hope Nixon can cool tensions in America and bring the troops home.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l124.c32/: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. You still fought hard, and took Nixon to the brink as Kennedy did in 60.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l126.c32/: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. The crime and rioting took a toll on your campaign hard, and Nixon's law and order theme really hit home for many Americans.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l128.c32/: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. It seems liberalism very well might be over with this loss, as you have been crushed. A more moderate candidate in 4 years will likely be chosen.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l131.c27/: Your first course of action is to fix what Johnson caused. Vietnam and the riots need to be dealt with. Johnson might not like how you deal with it, but this is your administration, and you'll deal with it the way you do. Act quickly, or you just might become as unpopular as Johnson.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l133.c32/: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. To the shock of pundits countrywide, you beat Nixon and Wallace handily. The bombing halt and your inspiring words compared to Nixon must have won it for you.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l135.c32/: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. It seems America is ready to give the New Deal Democrats one last chance. If you succeed, you might be able to rebuild the coalition that's won them so many elections (well, not the Deep South, but you knew that).
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l137.c32/: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. He did quite well, however, so you best work hard, lest the midterms act mercilessly.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l141.c23/: As expected, you lost the 1968 election
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l142.c23/: What happens next is your choice. Another governorship wouldn't hurt, and perhaps you can run again in 4 years if you're up to it. Unfortunately (for you), civil rights will persist.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l148.c32/: In a shock to all parties involved, neither Hubert Horatio Humphrey nor Richard Milhous Nixon will be the next president of the United States. Somehow, you managed to come out on top. Southerners are ecstatic, liberals are foaming at the mouth, and the black population has never been more fearful.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l149.c31/: Pundits are shocked, trying to figure out how you managed to capture states outside the deep south to win it all. What happens next is entirely unknown. Its likely a crusader against the civil rights bill will happen, as well as the deconstruction of Great Society, and the escalation of Vietnam. Whatever happens, sit back and relax knowing you've done the greatest upset in US political history!
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l152.c32/: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You did, however, come very close, picking up a number of states you weren't expected to pick up. It seems that your crusade for the south turned out really well. You could run in four years perhaps, and try and win the same coalition, trying to deadlock the election then. You've sent a clear message to the Democrats; the south isn't to be ignored,
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l154.c32/: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You did, however, poll a bit higher above what you were set to win. So good job outdoing your predictions. The south isn't done yet, as you've shown here.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/ending/s0.l156.c32/: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You won just about as much as expected, and yet it wasn't enough. Your supporters are disillusioned that you weren't able to deadlock the college. That's how it is, though...
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/327@: What is the overall theme of your campaign, remembering that the Democratic Party is underfunded and severely divided?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/328@: What will you say in your acceptance speech at the Democratic Convention in Chicago? Will you address the rioting outside and the legacy of Robert Kennedy?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/256@: Are you satisfied with the progress of desegregation in this country since the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/330@: Richard Nixon, perhaps remembering the debacle of 1960, has expressed little interest in a debate this election. Will you challenge him to one?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/338@: What is more important for your campaign -- competing with Nixon in the swing states, or winning over Wallace voters in the south and some northern cities?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/254@: What is your opinion of Lyndon Johnson's new Medicare program?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/252@: What is your overall position on the Vietnam War?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/255@: Are you satisfied with this nation's economic performance over the previous five years?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/253@: If elected, what will you do to get the student and Negro riots in this country under control?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/292@: Do we need more spending in the War on Poverty, especially in light of the riots since 1965?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/289@: Would you consider a constitutional amendment to outlaw the birth control pill, given the Supreme Court's decisions on that issue?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/265@: Should Lyndon Johnson have been able to prevent the Tet Offensive?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/283@: What do you think of the late Dr. Martin Luther King?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/291@: Do you believe that President Johnson overstepped his bounds in negotiating the Kennedy Round of trade agreements? Do you support the liberalization of international trade under the GATT?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/261@: What is your opinion of the military draft that is currently in place?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/287@: How would you prevent campus incidents like the takeover of Columbia University that occurred this past spring?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/259@: With all of the new programs that have implemented over the past five years, do you still believe there is room for the federal government to expand its responsibilities?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/270@: Are you concerned with some of the activist stances that Earl Warren has taken in his time with the Supreme Court?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/269@: What is your stance on the Six-Day War that occurred last year, and how should Israel handle the new territories it has taken possession of?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/264@: Do you believe that the black community in most cities overreacted to the assassination of Martin Luther King this past April?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/257@: Would you be willing to call an unconditional bombing halt of North Vietnam in the hopes of restarting peace negotiations?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/274@: Did the Supreme Court overstep its bounds in Loving v. Virginia by declaring state miscegenation statutes unconstitutional?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/288@: Do you hope to achieve an arms control agreement with the Soviet Union during your time in the Oval Office? What conditions would you agree to?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/284@: What is your position on expanding the Clean Air Act of 1963? Do you believe that stricter enforcement against pollutants is necessary, or does the current law suffice?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/questions_json/333@: On the weekend before the election, Lyndon Johnson's peace negotiations have collapsed with the North Vietnamese. Even worse, there are rumors that a Nixon operative has sabotaged the negotiations. Nixon swears to you on his honor that he is innocent. Will you make this an issue over the last two days of the campaign?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1653@0: We keep emboldening the enemy in Vietnam with half-measures. We will never win this war unless we escalate it.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1654@1: I'm in no position to comment on the conduct of the war. When I'm President I will do everything in my power to seek peace, but I cannot undermine the current Administration.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1655@2: We should stop bombing North Vietnam and attempt to negotiate a peace settlement. In the mean time, we should be putting our troops at risk only when absolutely necessary.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1656@3: We need to pull our forces out of Vietnam as soon as possible. This war is a national disgrace.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1657@4: There has been a total abdication of responsibility in this country over the past five years. The riots in Detroit and Newark are simply the final straw in what we can accept. I will crack down severely on disorder and nominate judges who will overturn atrocious decisions such as Miranda v. Arizona.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1658@5: Law and order is the primary theme of my campaign. We also need to encourage investment in the ghettoes to ensure a high quality of life and prevent these occurrences.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1659@6: Our first priority is always to have strong law enforcement. We also need more spending on education, more integration in our schools, and more programs to ensure that blacks can advance in our society after the stain of segregation.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1660@7: If we had peace in Vietnam and more investment in education here at home, we wouldn't be having these riots.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1661@8: Medicare is the first step towards socialized medicine in this country. We need to end this program as soon as possible and return health care to the states and to the people.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1662@9: We need to be very cautious about this program. It's important to ensure that the indigent can receive care, but programs like these always run the risk of adding precipitously to our national deficit.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1663@1: I commend this piece of legislation. Already we see many Americans receiving health care who would otherwise be stricken with serious and/or fatal conditions.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1664@1: Medicare is only the beginning of what we need to do in this country. I support a national health care system for all Americans.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1665@1: How can anyone be satisfied with the course our nation has taken? Inflation is killing the value of the dollar and the gold standard itself is at risk. Unemployment is highest under the Johnson Administration among the very people he claims to care about the most.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1666@1: Our current economic path is not sustainable. We need to continue the growth we have seen but we cannot allow this inflation we have to continue.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1667@1: The unemployment rate right now is under four percent. Workers, particularly those in labor unions, enjoy high purchasing power and an ever-expanding lifestyle. Economic growth throughout the 1960s has been outstanding.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1668@1: The worst thing we can do right now is to sabotage the progress we have seen by continuing to squander our money on a war in Vietnam. I support a full employment economy as well -- meaning we must be vigilant against misguided attempts to raise interest rates.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1669@1: Whites and Negroes are naturally unsuited to mix together in society. The entire premise of desegregation is a farce, and my campaign is dedicated to ending this misguided policy.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1670@1: I strongly support what we have done to end the insidious practice of segregation in the South. However I'm also alarmed at some of the ideas I've heard about forced integration of neighborhoods, or the proposed busing of students to distant schools.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1671@1: We have achieved great strides on this issue in the past twenty years -- and let the record show that Hubert H. Humphrey was at the forefront of this movement as early as 1948. We still have a long way to go, however, before we can truly realize the dream of Martin Luther King.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1672@1: We need to be very aggressive in fighting racism and its effects where they exist. I support programs such as busing, affirmative action, the new HUD department, and anything else that is necessary to integrate all regions of the United States.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1673@2: If anything, we need to escalate the bombing of North Vietnam. I don't go to bed at night with the feeling that they truly respect the power of America.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1674@2: We will never win the peace in Vietnam by caving in to the Communists. I cannot support such an ill-conceived measure.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1675@2: I would be willing to take this step and see what develops. It is imperative that we end the war in Vietnam as soon as possible.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1676@2: We need to pull our forces out of Vietnam as soon as possible. This war is a national disgrace.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1681@2: My God, this is a truly frightening question. Responsibilities of government need to be turned over to the states, and the federal government needs to be drastically reduced in size.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1682@2: The Great Society is founded upon the best of intentions, but we cannot afford this growth in spending on wasteful programs throughout our government.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1683@2: I will do everything in my power to defend the Great Society initiatives that we have. In those cases where these programs fail to eradicate poverty, I will not hesitate to augment them.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1684@2: We still need a national health care system. We still need a federal education system. Our work is never finished as long as poverty exists in the United States.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1689@2: We need to make sure that our military is adequately filled with personnel. That being said, I would prefer to see a volunteer system in place. I'm confident that there are enough patriotic young men in this country to make that system work.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1690@2: The draft is evil and should be abolished. We would never need it in the first place if warmongers like Johnson hadn't gotten us into this mess over in Vietnam.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1697@3: The reaction that occurred should terrify any thinking American. Entire neighborhoods were burned and pillaged. They even looted their own storekeepers in many cities.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1698@3: That was a very tough event for many of us to take, no matter what our backgrounds were. I believe that more precautions should have been taken to keep things from getting out of hand, but we must also remember that most Negroes wanted no part of these riots.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1699@3: I believe that both the black community and the police overreacted in many areas. First and foremost, we must speak out against violence wherever it may occur -- and against whoever is the source of it.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1700@3: The Tet Offensive was an absolute disaster for the North Vietnamese. Why should it have been prevented?
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1701@3: I'm worried that for most or all of 1967, Lyndon Johnson repeatedly assured us that the North Vietnamese were on their last legs. It's difficult to assess the situation when we can't rely on the information that we have.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1702@3: We should have had greater security in those places where we were attacked. Let us not forget, however, that this attack greatly hurt the Viet Cong and was a victory for the United States.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1703@3: We could have prevented the Tet Offensive entirely if we'd never entangled ourselves in this Vietnamese quagmire.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1716@3: Israel has every right to these territories they now occupy. They were attacked from all sides by an enemy bent on their destruction.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1717@3: As President, I'm confident that all sides can come together and negotiate a long-term peace agreement. Certainly the return of the Sinai or the Golan Heights should not be off the table.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1718@3: I fully support Israel's right to defend herself. However, I believe that these territories should be returned to the Arab states as a first step towards peace negotiations.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1719@4: This business in Israel is no business of America. I wish them the best, but we should not be obtrusively inserting ourselves into these multilateral peace negotiations. Doing so will only serve to entangle us in the long run.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1720@4: Earl Warren is without a doubt the worst Supreme Court justice in the history of the United States. From Brown v. Board of Education up through the present day, he has been nothing but an agent of tyranny for the federal government.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1721@4: On the balance I would not appoint another justice like Mr. Warren. Desegregating our schools was one thing, but he has gone off the deep end on these issues like school prayer, Miranda rights, and other activist decisions.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1722@4: It would be better in some cases if we could get Congress to make these decisions, but I do support the stances Mr. Warren has taken on the Court.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1723@4: The Warren Court is the first Supreme Court in history which has had the guts to use constitutional law for the benefit of the common citizen. I will continue to appoint sound judges like Mr. Warren, Abe Fortas, and Thurgood Marshall.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1735@4: My God, someone has to step in and protect good order in this society. This is just another instance of federal judges taking control over an issue that's simply none of their business.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1736@4: I'm not going to comment on a decision like this one. I certainly don't support miscegenation laws by any means, but I also think the Court has to be careful about overstepping the rights of the states.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1737@4: I fully support the Supreme Court in this decision. I don't know how someone in 1968 can stand up and fight against two peoples' right to marry each other.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1768@4: Dr. King bamboozled a lot of decent Americans with his rhetoric. I don't condone what happened to him, but most people fail to realize that he was a radical redistributionist and a borderline Communist.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1769@4: Dr. King is an American hero. I'm proud of his efforts to desegregate the southern schools and businesses, and I was deeply affected by his tragic demise this year.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1770@5: We need to continue to fight for the legacy of Dr. King. The continuing poverty of the blacks in our cities and in the South is a sobering reminder of how much work is left to be done.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1771@5: This is another case of pointy-headed intellectualism that will regulate our factories right out of business and kill the jobs of the working man.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1772@5: We need to find a balance between protecting the environment and protecting our economy. I support this Act but we also need to enforce it in a practical manner.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1773@5: I dream of a country where every citizen has clean air to breathe. The Clean Air Act is a good start but I'm not opposed to further legislation in this area.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1779@5: How these students have not been expelled is beyond me. If Administrators want to be complicit in the degradation of a private university, that is their own business. However, I won't spend a dime of federal money on a school that coddles radical agitators.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1780@5: I will crack down on dope-smoking, homosexuality, LSD binging, illegal protesting, and flag-burning. These practices are the tools of left-wingers and Communists who wish to undermine our society.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1781@5: There are some legitimate complaints behind these abhorrent actions. I will work for peace in Vietnam and civil rights in the United States. In the meantime, I support the rights of university administrators as they combat this problem.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1782@5: An arms control agreement with the Soviet Union isn't worth the paper that it's signed on. I won't participate in that kind of a charade.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1783@5: I would be open-minded about this issue. Without a clear statement of good faith, backed by concrete action, I have a hard time believing that the Soviet Union will come around to arms control.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1784@5: I will definitely work towards the control of nuclear weapons as President. I sincerely hope that we can work out a reasonable agreement on this issue.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1785@6: My goal is a world without nuclear weapons. While being mindful of reality, I hope to negotiate an expansive agreement that can put an end to the arms race.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1786@6: The Pill does not augur well for the social health of this nation. If we could get the support I'd love to see an Amendment that settles this issue once and for all.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1787@6: We have bigger priorities to deal with right now in America. I don't think that most Americans support or expect this kind of an initiative.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1792@6: International trade will undermine the prosperity of the working man as quickly as it will undermine the sovereignty of the United States. I don't support any of these global organizations.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1793@6: I support the overall thrust of this policy. Foreign trade supports our Cold War allies, reduces the cost of goods in America, and supports a broader economic prosperity.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1794@6: I support these international trade negotiations, but we must be sure that we don't undermine the rights of our own unions with one-sided agreements.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1795@6: The War on Poverty is a national disgrace. It is a program that steals from the productive to finance the lazy and the shiftless.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1796@6: We need to focus less on handouts and more on encouraging initiative among our black and ethnic business owners. They will build the prosperity in our inner cities. I will analyze the War on Poverty on a program-by-program basis and cut those which are unnecessary.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1797@6: I support the War on Poverty as it stands. We have passed a lot of new initiatives and we should wait to see what effect they have. To me, cracking down on the law and order issues is more important.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/1798@6: We are the greatest nation on earth and we cannot rest until every citizen has an opportunity to share in that prosperity.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/3251@7: For two decades I have fought for organized labor and supported the Civil Rights movement. I will focus heavily on my biography as I travel.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/3252@7: I will reaffirm my support for the Great Society and pledge to do everything in my power to end the Vietnam War.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/3253@7: The Johnson Administration has done a lot of good things for this country. I will continue his policies as President.
1968_Humphrey_Harris/answers_json/3254@7: First and foremost, I will end the war in Vietnam by any means necessary. Beyond that I will support the AFL-CIO and otherwise bear the standard for liberalism in this country.
